That the Committee recommends that Council: 1. ADOPT the amended Use of Local Government Property and Public Places Policy at Attachment 2. 2. NOTE that supporting information will be published on the Town's website with respect to Parklet and Alfresclets.
The proposed amendments clarify Council's position on parklets and alfresclets in response to increased interest from the local business community and recent activation projects within the Town.

The amendments explicitly recognise parklets and alfresclets as permissible where impacts on parking, amenity and revenue are acceptable, and provide additional flexibility for outdoor dining and the installation of fixed furniture in the public realm where safety and accessibility are maintained.
Moved by Cr MacRae, seconded by Cr Anderton

That in accordance with the provisions of the Town of Cambridge Town Planning Scheme and the Metropolitan Region Scheme and having regard to the matters it is required to consider by the Schemes generally and in partic ular as the proposal would be contrary to the orderly and proper planning of the locality by virtue of:- (i) the use of the property as Da y Centre for the Aged would representing an 'ad hoc' incursion of non residential activity into a residential area and establishing an undesirable precedent for further non residential uses along Salvado Road to the detriment of the established residential locality; the Council refuses the application submitted by Parry & Rosenthal Architects on behalf of the Sisters of Mercy for the construction of a Day Centre fo r the Aged on Lot 823 (No.124) Salvado Road, Wembley, as shown on plans submitted and dated 30 August 1996.

That the application submitted by [private individual — name withheld] to conduct a private function in the Garden Week area of Perry Lakes Reserve on Friday, 31 December 1999, be approved subject to :- (i) the charges for the conduct of the event to be as follows: (a) $600 hire fee, (b) $1000 reserve bond, (c) $50 outgoings (electricity, water); (ii) the sound levels associated with amplified music from the event, when measured at the boundary of the closest residence, not to exceed:- (a) before midnight - 65 dB(A) when measured as L Aeq, 1 min values; (b) after midnight - 55 dB(A) L Aeq, 1 min values; the organisers or their agent to establish compliance with the maximum permitted sound levels by regular measurement at the boundary of the closest residence; (iii) a liquor licence is to be obtained from the Liquor Licensing Court and a copy forwarded to Council prior to the event; (iv) the organisers or their agent to ensure that: (a) the supply and handling of food, (b) the provision of sanitary facilities, (c) all public and electrical safety issues, (d) all emergency management and fire safety issues, and (e) the responsible service of alcohol (in accordance with the terms of the Western Accord); (f) the clean up of the area the following day; comply, or are carried out in accordance with the Council's requirements; (v) the organisers or their agent to provide the Council with proof of a Public Liability Policy to the value of $10 million for the event; (vi) the use of fireworks be approved, subject to adequate safety precautions to the satisfaction of the Chief Executive Officer, being observed.

(i) the report detailing the August/September 2007 community consultation for traffic management in Pandora Drive and Malton Place be received;
